Empirical Research Plan  
“Liability Risk and Corporate Behavior, 1988–1999”

--------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  
--------------------------------------------------
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study extension.

Justification  
•  A single, well-defined law sharply raised liability exposure for a subset of public firms while leaving otherwise similar firms unaffected.  
•  The law’s passage date is common to all firms → clean “before/after.”  
•  The assignment rule (which firms are newly exposed) is plausibly exogenous to contemporaneous corporate outcomes.  
•  Annual panel (1988-1999) with many pre- and post-years → can test for parallel trends and estimate dynamic effects.

--------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control  
--------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Treat_it = 1 if firm i belongs to an industry–characteristic pair that the statute explicitly targets AND year t ≥ LawYear; 0 otherwise.

Concrete example (for illustration)  
If the statute expanded product-liability exposure for consumer-facing durable-goods producers, then:  
Treat_it = 1 for SIC codes 25xx, 32xx, 35xx, etc. after 1992; 0 otherwise.

Control group  
Firms that (i) operate in industries the statute exempts and (ii) are otherwise comparable on size, leverage, R&D intensity, and pre-trend outcomes. Primary control = all non-targeted manufacturing and service firms. Secondary controls = matched firms via propensity scores.

Timing  
Law enacted November 1991, effective fiscal year 1992.  
Pre-period: 1988-1991 (4 yrs).  
Post-period: 1992-1999 (8 yrs).

No running variable → not an RDD.

--------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
--------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: Absent the law, treated and control firms would have continued on similar outcome trajectories.  
– Plausible? Yes, because industries were chosen for legal, not economic, reasons. Will be checked via pre-trend event-study coefficients.

A2. No anticipation: Firms could not perfectly forecast the statute far enough in advance to change behavior prior to 1992.  
– Plausible because the final bill language changed repeatedly and passage was uncertain until late 1991.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): One firm’s liability shock does not alter another’s outcomes except through aggregate channels already absorbed by year FE.  
– Reasonable given the legal change is industry-specific and nationwide.

A4. Composition stability: The law does not differentially induce exit or entry that changes sample composition.  
– Will be tested by tracking attrition and including inverse-probability weights.

--------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations  
--------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential pre-trends.  
•  Mitigation: Graph event-study coefficients (–5 to –1 lags); include firm-specific linear trends; re-weight controls via entropy balancing.

T2. Contemporaneous shocks correlated with targeted industries (e.g., early 1990s recession).  
•  Mitigation: Industry-by-year FE at 2-digit SIC; control for regional demand shocks (state-year unemployment); placebo using outcomes unlikely to be affected by liability (e.g., effective tax rate).

T3. Misclassification of exposure (measurement error).  
•  Mitigation: Construct two alternative exposure measures (statutory text mapping vs. litigation-based ex-post measure); show robustness.

--------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline (executable)  
--------------------------------------------------
```r
############################################################
# 0. Packages
############################################################
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)      # fast TWFE regressions
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)

############################################################
# 1. Load data
############################################################
firm <- read_csv("firm_master_1988_1999.csv")      # Compustat-CRSP merge
law  <- read_csv("liability_law_industry_map.csv") # SIC codes affected

############################################################
# 2. Construct variables
############################################################
data <- firm %>% 
  mutate(post      = ifelse(year >= 1992, 1, 0),
         treated_i = ifelse(sic %in% law$sic, 1, 0),
         treat     = treated_i * post) %>%     # DID interaction
  mutate(ln_assets = log(at),
         capx_int  = capx/at,
         emp_gr    = (emp - lag(emp))/lag(emp)) %>%
  group_by(gvkey) %>% arrange(year) %>% ungroup()

############################################################
# 3. Baseline TWFE DID
############################################################
did_capx <- feols(capx_int ~ treat + ln_assets + leverage + roe | gvkey + year,
                  cluster = ~gvkey, data = data)
etable(did_capx, digits = 3)

############################################################
# 4. Event-study (-5,…,+8)
############################################################
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(event_time = year - 1992) %>%          # 0 = first treated year
  filter(event_time >= -5 & event_time <= 8)

event <- feols(capx_int ~ i(event_time, treated_i, ref = -1) + ln_assets |
               gvkey + year, cluster = ~gvkey, data = data)
iplot(event)

############################################################
# 5. Robustness: firm-specific trends
############################################################
did_trend <- feols(capx_int ~ treat + ln_assets + leverage + roe |
                   gvkey + year + gvkey::year, cluster = ~gvkey, data = data)
etable(did_capx, did_trend)
```

--------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results  
--------------------------------------------------
Theory suggests higher liability risk raises expected costs of hazardous or error-prone activities, lowering investment in risk-laden projects, slowing employment growth, and increasing precautionary cash holdings.  
Magnitude (illustrative): –5 % to –10 % reduction in cap-ex intensity and employment growth in the first three post-years; +3 pp increase in cash-to-assets.

--------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
--------------------------------------------------
C1: Parallel pre-trends visually/documented ……………… 1  
C2: No anticipatory effects (placebo leads ≈ 0)…………… 1  
C3: No time-varying composition/selection ………………… 0.5  
C4: Appropriate control group (similar covariates)……… 0.5  
C5: Correct inference (clustering, serial corr.)…………… 1  
Total = 4/5 → good but pre-trend & composition require scrutiny.

--------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
